migration_summary: ADD COLUMN with NOT NULL and a DEFAULT on older PostgreSQL rewrites every row (backfill); newer versions may optimize constant defaults as metadata-only, but applications must still treat this as a potential full-table rewrite.
migration_sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
schema_summary: Large users table; status column required by application immediately.

risk_flags.message: NOT NULL DEFAULT can rewrite all rows depending on engine version and default volatility.

risk_narrative: A defaulted NOT NULL column looks like a one-liner but historically rewrote the heap, holding locks proportional to table size—the same scaling law as index builds and generated STORED columns. Safe expand/contract uses nullable add, backfill in batches, then set NOT NULL.
lessons_learned: Split into expand (nullable) → backfill → constrain. Never assume ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT is metadata-only across all engines and versions. Measure on a shadow cluster sized like production.
surprise_notes: Teams often confuse this with nullable ADD COLUMN. The NOT NULL + DEFAULT combination is the backfill mechanism that should retrieve alongside hot-table index lessons.

prediction_summary.risk_explanation: Full-table rewrite risk scales with row count.
